units: <cite ref="Onkelos Numbers 24:9">Targ. Num. XXIV, 9</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 101b:14">B. Mets. 101ᵇ</cite>, a. e., v. <cite ref="A02950"><he>אֲרב</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Nedarim 62b:3">Ned. 62ᵇ</cite> <he>לאברוחי א׳</he> to drive the lion off, i.e. to get rid of the tax-collector.—
<cite ref="Shevuot 22b">Shebu. 22ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>א׳ הוא דרביע עלה</he> a lion lies on it, i.e. it is unavailable because it is forbidden.—
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 31b:11">Ab. Zar. 31ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <cite ref="A02006"><he>בר א׳</he></cite> son of a lion (of a great man).—

<cite ref="Chullin 59b:8">Ḥull. 59ᵇ</cite> the tiger is <he>א׳ דבי עילאי</he> the lion of the forest of Ilai (v. Schorr He-Ḥaluts VII, 32; cmp. Koh. Angelol. p. 103).—Pl. <he>אַרְיָוָתָא</he>, <cite ref="A03088"><he>אַרְיָוָן</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Targum of I Chronicles 11:22">Targ. I Chron. XI, 22</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:41">Lam. R. to I, 9</cite>) <he>א׳ דאורייתא</he> the lions of the Law (scholars). Y. Shebi. IX, 39ᵃ top.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:5:3">Y. Sabb. I, 4ᵃ</cite> top <he>מעלי רישא בין א׳</he> to put one’s head between lions, i.e. to argue against the opinions of great men. [<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 771:18">Yalk. Num. 771</cite> <he>גבתא דא׳</he>, v. <cite ref="A03093"><he>אֲרִיחַ</he></cite>.]
